It depends on entry price, leverage, the maintenance rate, the margin mode, and the fees and funding accumulated on the position, so it shifts over time rather than staying fixed. Isolated margin and cross margin produce different liquidation prices for the same trade.

records.en: Verify independently, and read what Openfund does not claim. That is verification of someone else's settlement layer, not evidence that Openfund settles on-chain, holds funds or runs proof of reserves - it claims none of those.

records.en: A block explorer is not a wallet, an exchange or an authority. It is a searchable index that reads the public ledger and lays one account or one transaction out on a page so a human can read it. That distinction matters, because everything trustworthy on that page is just a faithful copy of data that already exists on the chain - and everything you should be cautious about is any place the explorer adds its own interpretation. The right posture is to treat the page as a window, verify the view, and never confuse the window with the room.

Any reserves figure on the Transparency page is clearly labelled sample data, not production reporting, and the repository's Transparency rendering demonstrates a future interface, not a current balance.

When the count is reached you stop, because the rule was written while you were calm.

Those meanings are added around the data by whatever report or UI handed you the hash. Verification ends at the chain; interpretation beyond it is a claim to be checked against other evidence, not a fact the explorer owes you.

records.en: A static floor from the starting size is the friendliest of the three: you can lose the same distance again after a recovery, because the line does not move. A trailing boundary is the opposite - every new best equity raises it, so a rising account trades with progressively less room below. On the Instant terms of record the total drawdown trails at 5%, then locks at breakeven once the account is 5% in profit, and it does not reset after a payout. That shape rewards early restraint and punishes the instinct to size up after a good run.

records.en: These are the published Openfund challenge terms of record, none of which is purchasable or enforced in this release; the terminal currently runs the simulated demo. Standard: 5% daily loss (a 3% option) and a 10% static total. One-phase: 3% daily (a 2% option) and a 12% static total. Instant: a 5% trailing total drawdown that locks at breakeven once the account is 5% in profit. Free Trial: Standard rules, 14 days per phase. The daily limit is measured against the higher of day-start balance or day-start equity, resets at 00:00 UTC+3, and touching a limit is a breach. records.en: Where that leaves Openfund, stated without spin. Openfund offers code-level transparency: its source repository and documentation are public, and the perpetual view shows public Gains Network data you can inspect with a block explorer. It makes no financial-transparency claim: there is no proof of reserves, no published vault, no on-chain settlement and no customer-fund custody today, no independent audit has been completed (independent review is planned), the Certik PDF in the repo is an upstream report on a dormant third-party module and not Openfund's audit, and the Transparency page renders clearly labelled sample data, not production reporting. Liquidity aggregation across venues and intelligent order routing are future product directions, never current features. Telling that code apart from unproven finances is the point of this path.

records.en: A chain cannot see the world, so on-chain finance borrows prices from an oracle or index feed and trusts the result. Everything downstream - mark prices, collateral valuations, liquidation triggers - is only as correct as that borrowed input. When the feed is stale or wrong, immutability becomes a liability: the mistaken liquidation is now permanent and perfectly verifiable. That is the most common way on-chain transparency misleads - you admire how tamper-proof the recorded price is while nothing checks whether it was true.

records.en: Cross margin lets every open position draw on the same shared balance as collateral, so profitable or free positions cushion losing ones. It lowers each position liquidation price because more equity backs it, but it links their risk: one severe move can consume the whole balance and liquidate everything at once. Isolated margin is the alternative that ring-fences collateral to a single position.

records.en: Open interest is the total number or value of contracts that remain open. Every long must be matched by a short, so it counts both sides and never favours one: rising open interest with price signals new money entering, while falling open interest signals positions being closed. It measures how crowded a market is, not which way it will move, and not every data feed exposes it.

Everything the report never saw is as risky as it was.

records.en: Expectancy is the average amount a strategy earns or loses per trade across a large number of trades. It is computed as win rate times average win minus loss rate times average loss: p × avgWin − q × avgLoss. records.en: In isolated mode each position gets its own pocket of collateral. That pocket can be lost and nothing more: if price reaches the liquidation level, the venue closes that one contract and the damage stops at the edge of the pocket. The cost of the wall is that the pocket is small, so adverse movement has little fuel before it hits the limit. Adding margin to a losing position is then a deliberate act: risking more on an idea already wrong.

records.en: The project is organised around two trading products that share one workspace but never share money. Openfund Prop is a trader-evaluation product: traders practise and are evaluated on simulated accounts under published rules, and successful traders can earn rewards. Openfund Perpetual is a wallet-native product that reads a trader’s own positions on Gains Network. Around them sit the public website, a learning centre, a challenge catalog, wallet sign-in, a content management system and an economy layer that reports sales, rewards, expenses and treasury positions from records rather than estimates.

records.fa: سلیقه به اندازهٔ اطلاعاتِ زیرِ خودش ارزش دارد. معامله‌گری که عمق، جریانِ سفارش و پوزیشن‌گیری را می‌خواند کاری می‌کند که قاعده به‌سختی کپی‌اش می‌کند. اما مبدأِ داده‌های بازار در دسترسِ اوپن‌فاند هرگز عمقِ دفترِ سفارش، open interest یا نوارِ معاملاتی را تأمین نمی‌کند — پلتفرم آن‌ها را دست‌نیافتنی نشان می‌دهد و تخمینشان هم نمی‌زند. پس قضاوتی اینجا که ادعا کند دفترِ سفارش یا interest را حس می‌کند، هرچقدر هم مطمئن به نظر برسد، بر هیچ بنا شده. سلیقهٔ صادق درونِ همان چیزی می‌ماند که واقعاً می‌بینی: مارکِ قیمت، کندل، و شرایطِ مکتوبِ خودت.
records.en: Discretion is only as good as the information underneath it. A trader who reads depth, order flow and positioning is doing something a rule cannot easily copy. But the market-data source available to Openfund does not supply order-book depth, open interest or a trade tape at all - the platform shows those as unavailable and does not estimate them. So a judgment here that claims to sense the order book or open interest is built on nothing, no matter how confident it feels. Honest discretion stays inside what you can actually see: the price marks, the candle, your own written conditions.

records.en: A block explorer reports from its own index of the chain, and that index can be stale, can mis-render a value, or can be an operator's copy rather than the ground truth. The fix is cheap and mechanical: paste the same hash into a second, independent explorer for the same network, or query a node directly, and confirm the block number and status agree. Two unrelated sources landing on the same answer is what turns "the page says" into "the chain says." A single confident screenshot, by contrast, remains exactly what it is - one opinion rendered as an image.

records.fa: نرخ برد ۴۵٪، میانگین سود ۳۰۰ و میانگین ضرر ۱۵۰ را بگیرید: ۰٫۴۵ × ۳۰۰ منهای ۰٫۵۵ × ۱۵۰ می‌شود ۱۳۵ منهای ۸۲٫۵، یعنی امید ریاضیِ ۵۲٫۵ در هر معامله. سپس بپرسید آیا این برتری از پسِ هزینهٔ خودش برمی‌آید — کارمزد، اسپرد و اسلیپیجِ هر رفت‌وبرگشت، ضرب‌در تعدادِ ورودها. امید ریاضی متعلق به راهبرد به‌همراه اصطکاکش است.
records.en: Take a 45% win rate, an average win of 300 and an average loss of 150: 0.45 times 300 minus 0.55 times 150 is 135 less 82.5, or 52.5 of expected value per trade. Then ask whether that edge survives its own cost — fees, spread and slippage per round trip, times how often you trade. Expectancy belongs to the strategy plus its friction.

records.en: Unrealized PnL is the current profit or loss on positions you still hold, recomputed on each price change and not yet booked to the balance. It becomes realized only when the position closes and the final price and fees are settled.

records.en: The words carry precise meanings. Notional value is the full market size of the position, meaning how much of the asset you effectively control. Margin is the slice of your own equity reserved against it. Leverage simply states how many times bigger the first is than the second, which is why raising leverage does not hand you a bigger position for nothing: it takes the buffer you were holding and converts it into exposure.

records.en: The strongest sentence in this field is also the most over-read: "the data is on-chain, so it cannot be tampered with." It is true, and far weaker than it feels. Immutability is a promise about the future of a record - once written, it will not be quietly rewritten. It says nothing about the completeness of the record, the accuracy of the inputs it was built from, or the honesty of whoever chose what to put on the chain. Transparency that lives entirely on-chain has real limits, and naming them is what keeps the term meaningful.

records.en: Verification is worth understanding precisely because it is narrower than it sounds. When an explorer marks a contract "verified," someone has published source code whose compiled bytecode matches what is deployed at that address. That is a real service: it lets you read the logic instead of guessing from transactions. But it says nothing about whether the logic is honest, reviewed, or will stay unchanged. A verified contract can contain a self-destruct, and an unverified one might be perfectly ordinary.

Its real meaning comes paired with average win and average loss, because those two — not the win rate alone — decide expectancy.

records.en: On an account with a loss boundary the reaction is dangerous, because the boundary is measured on equity: unrealised losses move you toward the line the moment they appear, before any position is closed. On the Openfund simulated demo the daily loss is measured against the higher of day-start balance or equity, resets at 00:00 UTC+3, and touching a limit once is a breach no later recovery undoes. The impulse to average down or size up after a loss is thus the shortest route from an ordinary losing day to an account-ending one.

records.en: Confirmation count and finality are different ideas that get conflated constantly. The count just tells you how many blocks now sit above yours, which is a measure of how much work would be needed to rewrite that part of the chain. Finality is a threshold on that work: past it, the community treats the block as irreversible. That threshold is a property of the specific chain and can change, so a page that shows "12 confirmations" is reporting a fact, while the decision to call the transaction settled is yours to make against that chain's rules.

records.en: Risk per unit is the distance from entry to stop, reward per unit the distance from entry to target; their ratio is the reward-to-risk figure. Planned money at risk comes from account equity × risk percentage, and the planned reward scales by the same ratio. With a win rate supplied, expectancy is p × average win − (1 − p) × average loss, expressed in money and in R multiples. The break-even win rate is risk ÷ (risk + reward); a fee-adjusted version treats the round-trip cost as extra risk.

records.fa: معیار کلی نسبتی از سرمایه را می‌دهد که نرخِ رشدِ لگاریتمیِ بلندمدتِ حساب را بیشینه می‌کند. در ساده‌ترین شکل این نسبت f = (p·b − q) / b است که در آن p نرخ برد، q مکملِ آن و b نسبتِ سود به زیان است. کِلیِ کامل حدِ تهاجمیِ ریاضی است و فرض می‌کند برآوردهای شما از مزیت دقیق‌اند؛ به همین بیشترِ فعالان بازار کسری از آن را به کار می‌برند — کِلیِ نیم یا کمتر — تا خطای برآورد را تحمل کنند و از ورشکستگی بپرهیزند.
records.en: The Kelly criterion gives the fraction of capital that maximises the expected long-run logarithmic growth rate of the account. In its simple form the fraction is f = (p·b − q) / b, where p is win rate, q its complement and b the win-to-loss ratio. Full Kelly is the mathematically aggressive extreme: it assumes your edge estimates are accurate, so most practitioners bet a fraction of it — half Kelly or less — to tolerate estimation error and avoid ruin.

records.en: Openfund context: a checklist is most valuable where the account has hard boundaries. On the simulated Prop Trading demo a daily loss is measured against the higher of the day-start balance or day-start equity and resets at 00:00 UTC+3, and touching a limit is a breach - so writing the size and the stop before the order is how you keep a single decision from reaching that line. A checklist and journal are process, not a shortcut: purchase activation, funded accounts and payouts are not enabled in this release, and nothing here is investment advice or a promise that discipline produces profit or passes an evaluation.

records.fa: عبارت «اثباتِ ذخایر» وزنی بیشتر از آن‌چهار‌چیزی که این روش تحمل می‌کند به دوش می‌کشد. در شکلِ صادقِ خودش، نشان می‌دهد که دسته‌ای نشانی که یک شرکت مدعیِ کنترلشان است، در یک لحظهٔ مشخص واقعاً مقدارِ موجودیِ معینی را در اختیار داشته‌اند. این واقعیتی واقعی و سودمند است — و همچنین بسیار باریک. بیشترِ سردرگمیِ پیرامونِ این ایده از آن می‌آید که کلمهٔ «اثبات» را اثباتِ توانِ مالی می‌خوانند، یا اثباتِ اینکه طلبِ مشتریان داده می‌شود، در حالی که چیزی که هرگز ثابت شده همان تصاحبِ دارایی در یک نقطهٔ زمانی است.
records.en: The phrase "proof of reserves" carries more weight than the technique can hold. In its honest form it is a demonstration that a set of addresses a firm claims to control actually held some balance at a specific moment. That is a real and useful fact - it is also a very narrow one. Most of the confusion around the idea comes from reading the word "proof" as proof of solvency, or proof that customers could be paid, when all that was ever demonstrated is possession of assets at a point in time.

records.en: Run it once and it stays with you. Lose 20% of 10,000 and you are left with 8,000. Returning to 10,000 means earning 2,000 on 8,000, which is 25%. Lose half and the required gain is 100%. The relation is convex, so the first few percent of loss are cheap and the deep ones are almost unaffordable. That, not discipline for its own sake, is the real argument for cutting a loss early — while the arithmetic is still on your side.

records.en: For a long, the liquidation price is the point where the loss from entry has eaten the posted margin down to the maintenance requirement, which gives (notional − margin) ÷ (quantity × (1 − maintenance rate)). A short uses (notional + margin) ÷ (quantity × (1 + maintenance rate)). If you do not supply your own margin, it is derived from leverage.

records.en: Scope matters. This release is read-only on perpetual markets and cannot execute on-chain, so an automated system here means analysis, monitoring and backtesting over the records, not live orders. The Prop Trading environment is a single server-side simulated demo funded once with 100,000 virtual DAI at live Gains Network mark prices, with purchase activation, funded accounts and payouts not enabled. Treat each backtest as a rehearsal, and the CSV journal analyzer and portfolio dashboard - fed by the account records - as tools for measuring a process, not evidence about results.

records.en: Keep the sample-size caveat beside the schema, not inside it. Ten trades will always produce a tidy-looking win rate and profit factor; on that few closes they are noise wearing the costume of a signal, and metrics computed only on trades that made it into your curated history carry a survivorship bias you cannot see. Openfund ships a trading journal and a portfolio dashboard fed by the server account records, plus a CSV-based journal analyzer in the Tools Center that computes these figures over an uploaded history - a place to see the numbers, not a source of advice. Nothing here is a recommendation, and keeping a journal is not a claim on profit or on passing any evaluation.

records.fa: backtest ادعایی دربارهٔ گذشته است، نه وعده‌ای دربارهٔ آینده. به‌اندازهٔ کافی پارامتر روی یک تاریخ تنظیم کنی، تنظیماتی می‌یابی که تاریخ را آرایسته نشان می‌دهند، چون نویزش را حفظ کرده‌اند نه مزیتش را. محافظش walk-forward است: روی یک پنجره بهینه کن، روی پنجرهٔ بعدی که برازش ندیده ببر و بچرخان. اگر اعدادِ خوب فقط داخلِ همان داده‌ای که رویش تنظیم شده‌اند سر دو می‌آورند، تو شرحِ سالِ پیش ساخته‌ای، نه فرآیندی برای سالِ بعد.
records.en: A backtest is a claim about the past, not a promise about the future. Tune enough parameters against one history and you find settings that flatter it by memorising its noise instead of its edge. The guard is walk-forward testing: optimise on one window, run it on the next window the fit never saw, and roll. If good numbers survive only inside the data they were tuned on, you have described last year, not built a process for next year.

records.en: A terminal is a picture of a state, not the state itself. The numbers on the screen are produced by code - a smart contract at an address - and a clean interface can describe that code faithfully while still hiding it from you. Transparency at this layer is not about pretty charts; it is whether you can reach the actual program that decides your balance.

records.fa: ژورنال معاملاتی دفترِ احساسات یا تابلوی امتیازِ برد نیست. جدولی کوچک و ثابت است که هر بار به شیوه‌ای یکسان پرش می‌کنی، تا هفته‌ها بعد بتوانی چند عدد حساب کنی و دقیقاً یک چیز را بر پایه‌شان عوض کنی. ارزشش تماماً از نظمِ ثبت کردن می‌آید: لحظه‌ای که فیلدها از معامله‌ای به معاملهٔ دیگر لیز بخورند، همهٔ سنجه‌های مشتق‌شده از آن‌ها هم لیز می‌خورند و سابقه بی‌صدا به تزئینات تبدیل می‌شود. هدف اینجا، کمینهٔ ساختاری است که هنوز سنجه‌های واقعی تولید کند.
records.en: A trading journal is not a diary of feelings or a scoreboard of wins. It is a small, fixed table you fill the same way every time, so that weeks later you can compute a few numbers and change exactly one thing based on them. Its value comes entirely from consistency of recording: once the fields drift from trade to trade, every metric derived from them drifts too and the record quietly turns into decoration. The goal here is the smallest schema that still produces real metrics.

records.en: Friction has to be subtracted before a day looks acceptable, so it is worth being precise about which numbers are whose. Those describe the simulator, not a venue’s price list, and they are not commercial fees.

records.en: Not everything you are asked to verify has a transaction. Openfund's Prop Trading demo is a server-side simulation: a completed demo trade is an application record priced from live mark prices, not a chain event, and there is no hash to look it up. The perpetual view reads public data of the Gains Network deployment on Arbitrum One, and that - the venue's own settlement - is the only thing here you can verify on-chain; the Openfund surface is read-only and executes nothing on-chain in this release. Treating a demo fill or a UI number as a verifiable transaction would be exactly the error this lesson warns against, and Openfund makes no claim that its records are on-chain proofs.

records.en: Risk of ruin is the probability that losses take you to a point where you can no longer trade. It is built from win rate, average win and loss, risk per trade and a chosen ruin threshold, and it rests on assumptions markets routinely break: independent trades, a constant edge, an unchanging risk fraction, no effect from gaps or funding. Read it as a conditional estimate, never a guarantee.

records.en: The Openfund terminal is a single workspace used by both products. It embeds the Vela charting engine, fed by an Openfund adapter for Gains Network candles and live prices, and adds market discovery, an order ticket, open positions, order history, a portfolio and a private journal. The product context decides which financial authority answers: the Openfund engine for Prop, the trader’s own wallet records for Perpetual.

records.fa: آخرین مرز میان دو ادعاست که شبیه به نظر می‌رسند. شفافیتِ سطحِ کد یعنی هر کسی می‌تواند مخزن، build، قراردادهای مستقرشده و سورس‌هایِ تأییدشده‌شان را بخواند؛ عینی، قابلِ بررسی و رو به استاندارد شدن. شفافیتِ مالی چیزِ دیگری است — اثباتِ ذخایر، حسابرسیِ مستقلِ قراردادهای خودت، و لایهٔ تسویه‌ای که بتوانی وضعیتش را راستی‌آزمایی کنی. هیچ‌یک از دیگری پی نمی‌آید: یک پروژه می‌تواند کدِ متن‌بازِ بی‌عیب منتشر کند و باز هم اثباتِ ذخیره‌ای نداشته باشد، حسابرسیِ خودش را نداشته باشد و سرمایهٔ مشتری‌اش را آن‌چین نگذارد.
records.en: The last limit sits between two claims that sound similar. Code-level transparency means anyone can read the repository, the build, the deployed contracts and their verified sources; it is concrete, checkable and increasingly standard. Financial transparency is different - proof of reserves, an independent audit of your own contracts, a settlement layer you can verify. Neither follows from the other: a project can publish flawless open-source code and still have no reserves proof, no audit of itself and no customer funds on-chain.

records.en: For example, assume a settled rate of 0.01% per interval with three intervals a day. On a 10,000 notional that is 1 per interval, and the annualised figure is 0.01% x 3 x 365, about 10.95%. Change the rate or the interval count and the whole number moves — these are hypothetical inputs, and the real values come from the market feed, not from this page.

records.en: Discipline becomes a routine you run rather than a mood you feel. Before the order you confirm the three numbers and that the setup sentence is true. While the position is open you act only on what was written; anything new is a fresh decision for the next session, made cold. After it closes you record whether you followed the plan and tag what you felt, so the journal can separate rule-following losses from impulsive ones - worth very different things over a sample even when the money column is identical.

records.fa: حداکثرِ افت، بزرگ‌ترینِ کاهش از یک قله تا درهٔ پس از آن در ارزشِ حساب است که به‌صورت درصدی از همان قله بیان می‌شود. این معیار عمق را می‌سنجد نه مدت را، و بازگشت نامتقارن است: افتی به بزرگیِ d برای جبران به سودی به اندازهٔ d / (۱ − d) نیاز دارد — همان ۱ / (۱ − d) − ۱ — پس یک افتِ ۵۰٪ی برای سربه‌سرشدن به سودِ ۱۰۰٪ نیازمند است. بسیاری از شرکت‌ها سقفِ ضررِ کل را به‌شکلِ قاعدهٔ حداکثرِ افت بیان می‌کنند؛ گاهی این قاعده به‌صورتِ شناور یک سطح اوج را دنبال می‌کند نه مقدارِ ثابتِ شروع را.
records.en: Maximum drawdown is the largest decline from a peak to the following trough in account value, expressed as a percentage of that peak. It measures depth, not duration, and recovery is asymmetric: a drawdown of size d needs a gain of d / (1 − d), which equals 1 / (1 − d) − 1, so a 50% drawdown requires a 100% gain just to break even. Many firms express a total loss limit as a maximum-drawdown rule, sometimes trailing a high-water mark rather than a fixed starting value.

records.en: Gross profit is direction × (exit − entry) × quantity × contract size. Open and close fees are charged on their own notionals, and funding is applied to the position value for the intervals you held. Net is gross minus both costs, and return on investment is expressed against the posted margin. The break-even exit solves the same expression for a net result of zero, so fees and funding are already inside it.

records.en: The spread is the difference between the best bid a buyer will pay and the best ask a seller will accept, so a round trip crosses it twice. It is a core cost of trading: a market order pays the spread immediately, while a limit order placed inside it can capture part of it. Spreads widen in thin or fast markets and vary by instrument and venue, so the same asset is not equally cheap to trade everywhere.

records.en: Proof of reserves is a disclosure in which a venue publishes cryptographic evidence — commonly a Merkle-tree snapshot of on-chain assets against anonymous user balances — that the assets it holds at least cover what it owes users. It speaks only to assets held versus liabilities owed at a moment in time: it does not prove solvency overall, because it omits off-chain debt, loans and the timing between snapshots. Openfund makes no proof-of-reserves claim in this release; the Transparency page shows explicitly labelled sample data, not live reserves or an audit.

records.en: The upgradable pattern complicates trust further. A proxy address is stable and well-known, but it only forwards to separate implementation logic that can be swapped underneath it. This is genuinely useful - bugs can be patched and features added - yet it means reading the source at the proxy today does not guarantee the behaviour tomorrow. The question a careful reader shifts to is not "what does this address do" but "who can change what it does, and under what process?" That question often has no answer readable from the chain.

It happens at a price derived from the mark price, so it follows the smoothed reference rather than the last trade. How the loss is realised — through a venue liquidation engine or a backstop auction — and whether a penalty applies differ by exchange.

records.en: Margin is the collateral you lock up to open and keep a leveraged position; it is not a fee and not the full cost of the trade. Its size relative to the notional sets your leverage, and the maintenance-margin floor built from it decides how far price can move against you before liquidation. Some models treat margin as deducted from balance, while others reserve it without reducing the balance, so check which one your account uses.

Market orders are the typical taker, but any resting order you lift pays the taker fee too, and the exact rate varies by exchange and volume tier.

records.en: Slippage is the difference between the price you expected when you placed an order and the average price you were actually filled at. It grows when your size is large relative to order-book depth or when the market moves fast, because a market order must then walk more levels. Limit orders and smaller, split entries reduce it, but a fill can then be partial or missed instead.

The reset time and the exact basis differ by venue, so read the specific rule rather than assuming one standard.

records.en: Cross mode pools the free equity of the account behind every open position at once, so a losing trade is measured against the whole balance and can absorb far more adverse movement before it is closed. That is also the danger: a position that would have died quietly in isolation now draws collateral out of the account, and in a fast market several positions can consume the shared buffer together. When the pool runs out, everything resting on it is liquidated, not just the trade that began it.

records.en: Discipline means many things, but for a process it means one: evaluate a decision on the facts you had when you made it, and refuse to let the result rewrite that verdict. Traders who judge every closed trade by its profit or loss learn the wrong lesson half the time - a sound plan stopped out on a random spike printed a loss, an impulsive lucky bet printed a win. Reward the bet and punish the plan and you slowly train yourself to be worse. The checklist exists to break that loop.

records.en: The first mistake readers make is treating an address and a hash as the same kind of thing. An address is a place - it holds a balance and a history and never changes ownership by itself. A transaction hash is an event - one signed instruction that the network accepted and ordered into a block. When someone says "check the transaction," they mean the hash; when they say "check the account," they mean the address. Reading the wrong one of the two will give you a page full of real numbers about the wrong subject.

records.en: A credible reserves report is built so that an outsider can re-check it rather than take it on faith. The usual mechanism signs a message from the addresses themselves, or publishes a Merkle tree whose leaves are individual balances and whose published root lets each holder confirm their own line without seeing anyone else's. Both designs answer the same question - can you independently confirm that these assets exist at these addresses - and both stop there. Nothing in the mechanism compels the publisher to reveal every address it controls, or anything it does not control on-chain.

records.en: Leverage lets a small deposit control a large position. If you put up margin to hold a notional many times bigger, every one-percent move in price becomes a much bigger percentage move in your equity. That cuts both ways: leverage amplifies gains and losses by exactly the same factor, and it brings the liquidation threshold closer.

records.en: Openfund is an example of exactly this split, said plainly. Its Perpetual Trading surface reads the public data of the Gains Network deployment on Arbitrum One and is read-only: on-chain order execution is not enabled in this release and Gains transaction execution is deliberately disabled by project policy until testnet contracts, simulation and validation exist. Inside the repository, the openfund-protocol module is a dormant, imported third-party contract foundation (upstream MUX, GPL-2.0) kept for study - not compiled at its imported HEAD, not deployed, not used by the app and not Openfund's live settlement layer. The Certik report shipped inside it is an upstream document about that third-party code, not an audit of Openfund, which has no independent security audit yet. None of this means the perpetual view is dishonest about its source - it is honest about reading Gains data - but honest data displayed is not the same as Openfund itself being on-chain-settled, and it is not.

records.en: Openfund status: purchase activation, funded accounts and payouts are not enabled in this release, and a final versioned agreement will be published before launch. Demo profit is not money owed to the trader, and trading the demo does not establish eligibility for a funded account. Every figure in this path is a published term of record.

records.en: The distinction earns its keep precisely here. Because this release is read-only on perpetual markets and cannot execute on-chain, a manual override is not a way to put a real order in; it is only a way to change what your process does, in the records. That makes it easier, not harder, to be honest: the only discretion that means anything is the discretion you can describe, justify and measure - everything else is a decision without a trace, and an untraceable decision cannot be reviewed, so it teaches you nothing.

records.en: A stop-loss is a trigger you set in advance that closes a position once the price reaches a defined loss level, converting into a market or limit order at that point. It caps how far a single trade can hurt you, but because the triggered order then enters the market, the exit price is not guaranteed: in a gap or a fast move the fill can be worse than your stop. Where and how tightly to place it — manual versus a hard order, and which price the trigger reads — depend on the venue rules.

records.en: The file is parsed in your browser, rows are validated, and net profit per trade is taken from the profit column, with fees subtracted when the file provides them. Trades are then ordered chronologically to build an equity curve for the drawdown figures, grouped by day for the per-day and consistency views, and split into winning and losing runs for the streak statistics. Profit factor is gross profit divided by gross loss, expectancy is p × average win − (1 − p) × average loss, and any row that cannot be parsed is listed rather than silently dropped.

records.en: Persistent distress around losses - sleepless nights, anxiety that follows you away from the screen, trading to escape how you feel rather than to act on a plan - is not a discipline problem fixed by a better checklist. A trading process organises decisions; it is not therapy, and a loss should never be framed as a reason to hurt yourself.

records.en: The mark price is the price a venue uses to value a position: unrealized PnL, margin requirements and liquidation checks all read it. It is built as the index price plus a bounded basis — typically a moving average of that basis — so it moves smoothly and is hard to push with one aggressive trade. The tradable last price can briefly differ from the mark; the mark, not the last print, decides whether you are liquidated.

records.en: The same closed-trade list also gives you streaks - runs of consecutive closes with the same sign. They are the part people feel most and read worst: a five-trade losing run feels like collapse even when expectancy is intact, and a six-trade winning run feels like genius even when it is ordinary variance. That is why the metrics above are stated as fractions over a count: a single streak, like a single trade, is one data point, and one data point is not evidence about a process.

records.en: The Kelly criterion gives the fraction of equity that maximises long-run growth when your probability and payoff estimates are correct. Treat it as a ceiling rather than a target. Fractional Kelly exists to price that error.

records.en: Two different uses of the same idea appear in the published terms. On the Standard and One-phase models, the base share is 80% on a bi-weekly cycle, and the monthly cycle pays 100% when there are seven profitable days and the consistency score is respected - so the higher share is bought with evidence of regularity. On Instant, seven profitable days inside each rolling thirty is a condition of the payout itself, alongside the 15% cap. Both are counted at day level, which means the same total profit can clear one design and fail the other depending on how evenly it was distributed.

records.en: The funding rate is a periodic payment exchanged between traders holding opposite sides — longs and shorts — not a fee paid to the exchange. When the perpetual trades above the index, longs pay shorts; when it trades below, shorts pay longs, and this cost discourages the crowded side and nudges the contract price back toward the index. The rate, the interval and any cap are set per venue, so the same position can carry different funding on different platforms.

records.en: If you trade an evaluation, the stop is not your only boundary. Under the published Openfund terms of record — not purchasable or enforced in this release — the daily loss limit is measured against the higher of day-start balance or day-start equity, resets at 00:00 UTC+3, and touching it once is a breach. Standard: 5% daily (a 3% option) and 10% static total. One-phase: 3% daily (a 2% option) and 12% static total. Instant: a 5% trailing total drawdown that locks at breakeven once the account is 5% in profit. A stop that saves the position but reaches the daily limit still costs you the account.

records.en: Read that ratio before anything else. Where the target is small relative to the total limit, ordinary losing weeks are survivable and the test is mostly about steadiness. Where the two are equal, one bad stretch consumes the entire allowance and the evaluation becomes a test of drawdown control first, profit second. Neither design is better; they screen for different behaviour, which is why both can honestly carry the same reward split.

records.en: These two ideas are often collapsed into one. A trading interface can be scrupulously truthful about where its numbers come from while the venue that actually finalises the trade is an entirely different on-chain deployment. Honest disclosure of the source is a virtue of the interface; the on-chain state it reflects belongs to the venue. Keeping them apart is what stops a well-labelled screen being mistaken for a settlement guarantee - the label says where the data came from, not who pays you if the numbers are right.

records.en: A perpetual future is a leveraged, collateralised contract that settles against an underlying price but has no expiry date, so you can hold it indefinitely. You never own the underlying asset; you hold a position whose value tracks the price up or down.

That gap between how a streak feels and how it scores is where discipline is tested: the feeling pushes toward action, the statistics advise waiting.

records.en: Risk of ruin is the probability that losses drive an account to a point from which it can no longer keep trading. It grows with per-trade risk and with how negative or thin your edge is, and shrinks as the bankroll grows relative to each bet. It is a statistical estimate under explicit model assumptions — fixed bet size, a given win rate and independent trades — so a low figure is not a guarantee, and a change in behaviour can invalidate the model.

records.en: Take an entry of 100 at 10x with a maintenance rate of 0.5%. Isolated, the long liquidates near 90: 100 * 0.9 / 0.995 is about 90.45, so roughly a 9.5% adverse move ends the trade and nothing else. Put the same position in cross mode with much more equity behind it, and that same 9.5% move is no longer a wall — it is a withdrawal from the account. The formula did not reward you with extra room; you simply relocated the loss from a position onto your balance.

Remaining room is the difference, and the breach check adds the open risk you type so you see the outcome before it happens.

It only relocates what the guarantee depends on. Once you notice that the mechanism is honest about one narrow thing and silent about everything else, you stop asking it questions it was never designed to answer, and start asking who signed the report, what scope they chose and how old the snapshot is.

records.en: None of this lifts the account terms off you: an automated strategy still inherits every loss limit and payout condition of the account it runs on. On the Openfund simulated demo a daily loss is measured against the higher of the day-start balance or equity, resets at 00:00 UTC+3, and touching a limit is a breach regardless of who placed the order. Consistency is a payout condition - 35% on the monthly path, 15% on Instant - so a system that packs profit into one run can clear the loss limits and still fail the gate.

records.en: Slippage is the difference between the price you saw when you decided and the average you actually got. It grows with your size relative to depth and with speed: a thin book or a fast move forces a market order to walk further down the ladder. Using limit orders, splitting size, or trading calmer hours reduces it, but never removes it.

records.fa: ورودی‌هایت به میانگین و واریانس بازده هر معامله در آن درصد ریسک تبدیل می‌شوند. سپس برآورد با تقریب رایج انتشار انجام می‌شود: P ≈ exp(−۲ × میانگین × ln(سرمایه ÷ سطح توقف) ÷ واریانس). در کنار آن، لبهٔ هر معامله، نسبت Kelly برای این ورودی‌ها و بیشترین درصد ریسکی که احتمال برآوردی را زیر ۵٪ نگه می‌دارد نمایش داده می‌شود.
records.en: Your inputs are converted into the mean and the variance of per-trade returns at the chosen risk fraction. The estimate then applies the standard diffusion approximation, P ≈ exp(−2 × mean × ln(capital ÷ stop-out level) ÷ variance). Alongside it you get the per-trade edge, the Kelly fraction for these inputs, and the largest risk fraction that keeps the estimated probability below 5%.

records.en: Openfund is building a connected trading and trader-funding ecosystem: one shared trading terminal, a server-authoritative evaluation engine, a published challenge catalog, wallet-native identity and an economy whose figures come from operational records rather than marketing. This paper describes what the project is, how it works, how it earns and spends money, how capital could one day reach real markets, and — just as importantly — which parts are live today, which are implemented but not yet released, and which remain plans.

records.fa: اهرم را دستهٔ کنترلِ مواجهه بدانید، نه دستهٔ بازده. اندازهٔ موقعیت، حالت وجه تضمین و فاصله‌تان از قیمت لیکوئیدیشن تعیین می‌کند که یک اصلاحِ عادی قابل تحمل است یا نه. درس‌های بعدی این اهرم‌ها را یکی‌یکی باز می‌کنند.
records.en: Treat leverage as an exposure dial, not a return dial. Sizing, margin mode and how close you run to the liquidation price decide whether a normal pullback is survivable. The next lessons take these levers one at a time.

records.fa: رول‌بوک‌ها کوتاه‌اند و دقیقاً به همین دلیل خیلی‌ها یک‌بار می‌خوانندشان و فکر می‌کنند بلدند. روشِ قابل‌اتکا پنج عبور است با یک سؤال در هر عبور: واژه‌ها چه معنایی دارند، هر عدد با چه چیزی سنجیده می‌شود، نقض چیست، پیش از پرداخت چه باید درست باشد و چه چیزی جا افتاده. این ترتیب روی سندِ هر ارائه‌دهنده‌ای کار می‌کند و همان ترتیبی است که فاصلهٔ میان «آنچه صفحه می‌گوید» و «آنچه تو فرض کردی» را آشکار می‌کند.
records.en: Rulebooks are short, which is exactly why people read them once and believe they know them. The dependable method is five passes, each asking one question: what do the words mean, what is each number measured against, what counts as a breach, what must be true before payment, and what is missing. That order works on any provider’s document, and it is the order that exposes the gap between what a page says and what you assumed.

records.fa: فاندینگ را مثل دماسنج بخوانید، نه پیش‌بینی. نرخ مثبتِ کشیده می‌گوید جمعیت خریدار است و برای ماندن می‌پردازد؛ اما نمی‌گوید قیمت به کدام سمت می‌رود. با این حال، هزینه‌ای که به موقعیت اضافه می‌کند حسابِ واقعی و قابل برنامه‌ریزی است.
records.en: Read funding as a thermometer, not a forecast. A stretched positive rate tells you the crowd is long and paying to stay so; it says nothing about which way price goes next. The cost it adds to a position, however, is real arithmetic you can plan around.
